people.gloss: The good rain that knows its season (Đỗ Phủ: hảo vũ tri thời tiết)
people.role: Abbess of Cốc Vũ Quán since 958: rain-calling rites and spirit-rice terraces for the farmers of the south
people.appearance: A small, brown, smiling woman in a patched grey robe and a rice-straw hat, with mud to the knee and a cough she hides in her sleeve.
people.backstory: Dương Hảo Vũ was born in 830 in a drought year at Phong Đăng, to tenants on the Lục family's farms, whose harvests the Tower taxes first (A288). The abbey's rain came the week she was born, and her mother named her for it. She went up the bamboo hill at ten. The founder Hạng Đảo Vũ (hang_dao_vu) was a rain priestess from the coast who called rain with Water, and by then the hill had stopped answering her. When the founder died in 958, Dương became abbess. She spent forty years learning to call rain the other way: not from the sea, but from the forest's own breath (N-coc_vu-02). It worked, and the farmers have had their rain since. In the great drought of 1150 she held the Grain Rain rite for nine days over the farmers' valleys of Phong Đăng and Ương Ca and not over the Tower's terraces. The Tower's rice failed, and it marched on Đan Sơn Mạch's cinnabar to pay for grain (C188). Her meridians have not been right since. In 1093 she stood at Thu Phần's graves and felt the chorus drawn up the way her own rite draws the forest's breath, and since then her autumn rice to the Pavilion has been a price, paid so that the river's drowned are left to rest. Its founder, Lý Hận Bích (ly_han_bich), was born the same year as she was. In 1180 half the abbey walked out to the grove with Hà Tĩnh Cần (ha_tinh_can), and the abbess struck none of them off.
people.wants: Rain for every planting and no rain sold; her abbey whole again; and the dead of Lôi Trạch at rest before she is.
people.secret: Since 1180 everyone knows that the prior's pills are bought with sold rain, and she takes them. No one knows that since the spring she has kept back one in three and sent it to the grove for Hà Tĩnh Cần, who, the two villages that came back to pay told Lục Đạo Hoa, now holds each free rite twice and pays for it in years. The prior's pills are keeping alive the rival he pays to ruin.

people.role: Prior (giám viện) of the abbey: its stores, its tax, and the rain it sells at a posted price
people.appearance: A plump, pleasant monk with an abacus in his sleeve and the soft hands of a man who keeps the books.
people.backstory: A rice merchant's son from Thu Trì who came to the abbey at twenty and never quite stopped counting. Since 1010 he has sold the abbey's rain in dry years to Kiều Mãn Lâu (kieu_man_lau) and to any landlord who pays, and since 1150 the money has bought the pills that keep the abbess (duong_hao_vu) breathing. In 1180 Hà Tĩnh Cần (ha_tinh_can) told the valley, and half the abbey walked out with her. He posted the price on the gate the next morning. Now he pays the grove's pole-cutter Sở Lôi Duẩn (so_loi_duan) to cut the hermitage's poles a hand short, so that its free rites call drizzle and the farmers come back to pay.

His family's tenants send their children to the Tower's Bell Test first and to him when they fail, as the Thiều boy came. He does not mind being second.

people.appearance: A tall woman in a black rain cloak over the abbey's grey, who is seen in Thu Trì only on dry nights.
people.backstory: Born in Yên Vũ Trấn, the town of misty rain, she has the best rain hands in the abbey. In dry years the prior Thời Tri Tiết (thoi_tri_tiet) sends her to Thu Trì to call rain at dusk so that Kiều Mãn Lâu's (kieu_man_lau) market can open, and she stays to drink in it. In the dry year of 1179 Hà Tĩnh Cần (ha_tinh_can) called it beside her. Since 1180 everyone knows what the rain is for, and she goes on calling it.

people.role: Rite master who walked out of Cốc Vũ Quán in 1180; keeps the hermitage in Lôi Trúc Lâm and calls rain for nothing
people.appearance: A small, sun-dark woman in grey hemp gone white at the knees, with the pale mark of a rite bell's cord still on her wrist.
people.backstory: Born in 1040 to Lục tenants at Phong Đăng, she went up the bamboo hill at her first planting. Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu) made her master of the rite's callers. In the dry year of 1179 the prior Thời Tri Tiết (thoi_tri_tiet) sent her to Thu Trì to call the Night Rain Market's rain beside Lã Tiềm Dạ (la_tiem_da). She came home in the spring of 1180 to Phong Đăng's dead seedbeds, and at that planting she told the valley where she had been and what it was paid. Half the abbey walked with her to Lôi Trúc Lâm. She gave the abbess back her rite bell, and from the grove she calls rain for any farmer for nothing. This year three of her rites have come down as mist, and she now holds each one twice.

people.role: Founder of Cốc Vũ Quán (610): a coast rain priestess who called rain with Water
people.backstory: A rain priestess from the sea-spray coast who came inland in a drought and founded the abbey on a bamboo hill above Phong Đăng to call the rain for the farmers and grow spirit rice (V154). She called rain from the sea with Water, and it came for three hundred years. The hill held no Water of its own, and it came less each century. She died in 958, in a dry year, under the last rain she called. Her disciple Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu) learned to call it from the forest instead.

ties.note: her successor
